name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah steady near record lows around 18,260/$ after Bank Indonesia's 18 Nov rate rise; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: The rupiah closed at 18,255 per dollar on 19 Nov (Bisnis Indonesia), with a reference rate of 18,275 that day (Databoks), close to the record low near 18,290 set before Bank Indonesia raised its rate to 6% on 18 Nov. The currency has held roughly steady since the rise and is about 9% weaker this year, short of a 10% fall in a month. No major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 22 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: A strong dollar and higher US rates keep pressure on emerging-market currencies, raising import costs and dollar-debt burdens there. Travellers to Indonesia get more rupiah per pound.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month, no default or IMF rescue = Normal

sources.title: Bisnis Indonesia — Rupiah ditutup melemah ke Rp18.255 per dolar AS (19/11)
Databoks — Rupiah exchange rate weakens to IDR 18,275 per US dollar

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
